LESSON: VISUAL PROGRAMMING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.2: Visual Programming
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Visual Programming, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How are applications developed using visual programming software?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the application areas of visual programming software in solving problems,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Visual Programming in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. create an application using visual programming software for solving problems in day-to-day life,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Visual Programming in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. embrace the use of visual programming in the day- to-day life. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print and non-print media to identify key terminologies related to visual programming. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to watch signed/captioned video clips or watch a demonstration on how to sign terms related to visual programming in solving problems. • In pairs, learners practise how to fingerspell and sign terms related to visual programming. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use digital devices and print media to search for information and captioned videos on How are applications developed using visual programming software? 20 application areas of visual programming software in solving problems. In cases where videos are not captioned, ensure the videos are supported by sign language interpretation and pause to allow the learner ample time to follow and interpret the videos. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Visual Programming together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: effective communication skills are developed as the learner discusses the application areas of visual

programming with peers.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: open-mindedness and creativity skills are developed as the learner develops an

application using visual programming software.

Value:

Social justice: learner shares resources equitably with others as they work in groups to develop applications.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

22

● Peer Education and Mentorship: interpersonal relationships is enhanced as learner discusses the application areas of visual

programming software.

● Internet Safety and Security: responsible online behaviour is enhanced as learner uses available resources to search for

information on the application areas of visual programming.

Link to other subjects

Creative Arts: learner enhances skills of animations when developing interactive stories, games and animations.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Digital devices.

• Print media.

• Animations.

• Manilla papers.

• Captioned video clips
